Sampled top-k success can conceal full-catalog failure: omitted high-scoring competitors improve apparent target rank. GRU4Rec experiments in [Hidasi and Czapp, 2023](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/eval_flaws_recsys23.pdf) demonstrate this distortion and derive sampled-hit probabilities from full rank using a hypergeometric distribution. [Pereira et al., 2025](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) examine sampling reliability through fidelity, resolution, robustness and recovery of model rankings. Strong margins against 99 negatives therefore provide limited evidence about catalog-wide top-10 placement.

Practical diagnostic proposal: freeze the single trained GRU4Rec per category and score eligible catalog items in chunks for the same validation histories. Record full target rank, rank displacement relative to sampled evaluation, sampled-hit/full-catalog-miss frequency, and target score minus the tenth-highest eligible competitor score. Count omitted competitors outranking the target. Independently redraw diagnostic sets of 99 unique negatives to estimate each user’s hit probability and aggregate sampling variability; bootstrap users separately to quantify uncertainty from user selection. Under uniform sampling without replacement, the hypergeometric calculation provides an analytic cross-check. These are descriptive probes, not changes to the pinned evaluator or selection metric.

Popularity-conditioned analysis is especially relevant: [Prakash et al., 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) find aggregate sequential-recommendation metrics hide head/mid/tail disparities, with random training negatives favoring head items in their experiments. Define popularity bands using training interactions only; report support counts, sampled/full hit rates, rank displacement and competitor popularity within each band and category. Treat unobserved items as competitors, not verified dislikes. Keep all diagnostic results separate from the unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10; no test labels, retraining, auxiliary predictor or score fusion required.
